--
## Context

Two finished subsystems aren't connected yet:

- the quality report flags `duplicate_candidate` pairs ([`quality_checks.py`](backend/app/services/quality_checks.py)), but offers only *dismiss* — no way to act on a real duplicate;
- [`merge.py`](backend/app/services/merge.py) already has `compute_merge_preview` and per-pair, per-field conflict `resolutions` (#166) — but only for **tree-level** merges that produce a brand-new tree.

Merging two members *within* a tree currently means manually re-wiring relations and links, then deleting one row. Duplicates are the most persistent data-quality problem in genealogy.

## Goal

A guided in-place merge of two members of the same tree, launched from a `duplicate_candidate` finding in the quality-report view (and optionally from member selection in the tree).

## Scope

- **Backend**: `POST /trees/{tree_id}/members/merge` taking `(keep_id, remove_id, field resolutions)`:
  - preview endpoint first (reuse/extract the field-conflict logic from `compute_merge_preview` rather than forking it);
  - union relations (dedup, drop self-relations), re-point parent references (`maternalParent`/`paternalParent`) of children, transfer event/story/gallery/document/disease links, keep the chosen photo, combine notes;
  - guard rails: both members in the same tree, refuse merging a member with itself, refuse when it would create a relationship cycle (reuse the cycle check from quality checks);
  - `record_activity` with a rich payload — ideally the full pre-image, aligning with #572 so merges become reversible later.
- **Frontend**: "Merge…" action on `duplicate_candidate` findings in `QualityReportView` → dialog with side-by-side field comparison and per-field pick (shape borrowed from the tree-merge resolution UI), preview of what will be transferred, confirm.
- Entry point lives behind the existing `quality_report` flag; the endpoint itself is core member CRUD (not separately flagged).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Preview shows field conflicts and what will be transferred before anything is written
- [ ] After merge: all relations/links/content of the removed member are attached to the kept member, no dangling references, layout recomputes cleanly
- [ ] Cycle/self-merge guards with clear errors
- [ ] Activity log entry with enough detail to audit the merge
- [ ] Backend tests for relation re-pointing, link transfer, and guard rails
- [ ] i18n keys in every locale

326	    "combine", a = ``member``, b = ``counterpart``) from ``choices`` is
327	    applied when given; otherwise the fields are unioned (whichever side is
328	    non-empty wins, preferring ``member`` when both are set) via the same
329	    a/b/combine semantics as ``apply_field_choices``. ``image_data`` is copied

1	"""Data-quality checks for a family tree."""
2	
3	import hashlib
4	from collections import defaultdict
5	
6	from app.models.content import Event, EventMemberLink
7	from app.models.family import Member, Relation
8	
9	# Minimum/maximum plausible age of a parent at their child's birth.
10	_MIN_PARENT_AGE = 10
11	_MAX_PARENT_AGE = 100
12	
13	# A child can legitimately be born shortly after their *father's* death
14	# (a posthumous birth, up to ~9 months later). Dates here are year-only, so a
15	# one-year grace window is allowed for fathers and unknown-gender parents. A
16	# birth after the *mother's* death is not biologically possible, so mothers get
17	# no grace.
18	_POSTHUMOUS_BIRTH_GRACE_YEARS = 1
19	
20	# Event types that legitimately happen after a person's death and should not
21	# be flagged by the event-after-death check.
22	_POST_DEATH_EVENT_TYPES = frozenset({"burial"})
23	
24	
25	def _year(date_str: str | None) -> int | None:
26	    if not date_str:
27	        return None
28	    try:
29	        return int(date_str.split("-")[0])
30	    except (ValueError, IndexError):
31	        return None
32	
33	
34	def issue_id_for(issue_type: str, member_ids: list[str]) -> str:
35	    """Deterministic id for an issue, derived from its type and members.
36	
37	    Issues are recomputed fresh on every request rather than stored, so this
38	    id is what lets a dismissal survive across requests: as long as the same
39	    underlying data produces the same issue, it hashes to the same id.
40	    """
41	    key = f"{issue_type}|{','.join(sorted(member_ids))}"
42	    return hashlib.sha256(key.encode()).hexdigest()[:32]
43	
44	
45	def run_quality_checks(
46	    members: list[Member],
47	    relations: list[Relation],
48	    events: list[Event] | None = None,
49	    event_links: list[EventMemberLink] | None = None,
50	) -> list[dict]:
51	    events = events or []
52	    event_links = event_links or []
53	    issues: list[dict] = []
54	    member_map = {m.id: m for m in members}
55	
56	    # --- 1. Birth-after-death ---
57	    for m in members:
58	        birth = _year(m.date_of_birth)
59	        death = _year(m.date_of_death)
60	        if birth is not None and death is not None and birth > death:
61	            issues.append(
62	                {
63	                    "issue_type": "birth_after_death",
64	                    "severity": "error",
65	                    "member_ids": [m.id],
66	                    "description": f"Birth year ({birth}) is after death year ({death}).",
67	                }
68	            )
69	
70	    # --- 2. Parent–child age-gap anomalies ---
71	    # Relation direction: from_member_id = child, to_member_id = parent
72	    parent_pairs: list[tuple[str, str]] = [
73	        (r.to_member_id, r.from_member_id)  # (parent_id, child_id)
74	        for r in relations
75	        if r.relation_type == "parent"
76	    ]
77	
78	    for parent_id, child_id in parent_pairs:
79	        parent = member_map.get(parent_id)
80	        child = member_map.get(child_id)
81	        if parent is None or child is None:
82	            continue
83	        parent_birth = _year(parent.date_of_birth)
84	        parent_death = _year(parent.date_of_death)
85	        child_birth = _year(child.date_of_birth)
86	
87	        # Child born after the parent had already died. Fathers (and parents of
88	        # unknown gender) get a small posthumous-birth grace window; mothers get
89	        # none, since a birth after the mother's death is impossible.
90	        if parent_death is not None and child_birth is not None:
91	            is_mother = (parent.gender or "").lower() == "f"
92	            grace = 0 if is_mother else _POSTHUMOUS_BIRTH_GRACE_YEARS
93	            if child_birth > parent_death + grace:
94	                issues.append(
95	                    {
96	                        "issue_type": "child_after_parent_death",
97	                        "severity": "error",
98	                        "member_ids": [parent_id, child_id],
99	                        "description": (
100	                            f"Child was born ({child_birth}) after the "
101	                            f"parent's death year ({parent_death})."
102	                        ),
103	                    }
104	                )
105	
106	        if parent_birth is None or child_birth is None:
107	            continue
108	        age_at_birth = child_birth - parent_birth
109	        if age_at_birth < 0:
110	            issues.append(
111	                {
112	                    "issue_type": "child_older_than_parent",
113	                    "severity": "error",
114	                    "member_ids": [parent_id, child_id],
115	                    "description": (
116	                        f"Child's birth year ({child_birth}) is before "
117	                        f"parent's birth year ({parent_birth})."
118	                    ),
119	                }
120	            )
121	        elif age_at_birth < _MIN_PARENT_AGE:
122	            issues.append(
123	                {
124	                    "issue_type": "parent_too_young",
125	                    "severity": "warning",
126	                    "member_ids": [parent_id, child_id],
127	                    "description": (
128	                        f"Parent was only {age_at_birth} year(s) old when "
129	                        f"child was born ({child_birth})."
130	                    ),
131	                }
132	            )
133	        elif age_at_birth > _MAX_PARENT_AGE:
134	            issues.append(
135	                {
136	                    "issue_type": "parent_too_old",
137	                    "severity": "warning",
138	                    "member_ids": [parent_id, child_id],
139	                    "description": (
140	                        f"Parent was {age_at_birth} years old when "
141	                        f"child was born ({child_birth})."
142	                    ),
143	                }
144	            )
145	
146	    # --- 3. Relationship cycles (parent-chain) ---
147	    # Build child→parents adjacency for traversal.
148	    parents_of: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
149	    for parent_id, child_id in parent_pairs:
150	        parents_of[child_id].add(parent_id)
151	
152	    visited: set[str] = set()
153	    on_stack: set[str] = set()
154	    cycle_members: set[str] = set()
155	
156	    def _dfs(node: str) -> bool:
157	        visited.add(node)
158	        on_stack.add(node)
159	        for ancestor in parents_of.get(node, set()):
160	            if ancestor not in visited:
161	                if _dfs(ancestor):
162	                    cycle_members.update([node, ancestor])
163	                    return True
164	            elif ancestor in on_stack:
165	                cycle_members.update([node, ancestor])
166	                return True
167	        on_stack.discard(node)
168	        return False
169	
170	    for m in members:
171	        if m.id not in visited:
172	            _dfs(m.id)
173	
174	    if cycle_members:
175	        issues.append(
176	            {
177	                "issue_type": "relationship_cycle",
178	                "severity": "error",
179	                "member_ids": sorted(cycle_members),
180	                "description": "A cycle exists in the parent-child relationships.",
181	            }
182	        )
183	
184	    # --- 4. Duplicate-name candidates ---
185	    name_groups: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
186	    for m in members:
187	        first = (m.first_name or "").strip().lower()
188	        last = (m.last_name or "").strip().lower()
189	        if first or last:
190	            name_groups[f"{first}|{last}"].append(m.id)
191	
192	    for _key, ids in name_groups.items():
193	        if len(ids) > 1:
194	            issues.append(
195	                {
196	                    "issue_type": "duplicate_candidate",
197	                    "severity": "warning",
198	                    "member_ids": ids,
199	                    "description": f"{len(ids)} members share the same full name.",
200	                }
201	            )
202	
203	    # --- 5. Disconnected members (no relations at all) ---
204	    if len(members) > 1:
205	        connected: set[str] = set()
206	        for r in relations:
207	            connected.add(r.from_member_id)
208	            connected.add(r.to_member_id)
209	        for m in members:
210	            if m.id not in connected:
211	                issues.append(
212	                    {
213	                        "issue_type": "disconnected_member",
214	                        "severity": "warning",
215	                        "member_ids": [m.id],
216	                        "description": "Member has no relationships.",
217	                    }
218	                )
219	
220	    # --- 6. Event dated after the member's own death ---
221	    event_map = {e.id: e for e in events}
222	    for link in event_links:
223	        member = member_map.get(link.member_id)
224	        ev = event_map.get(link.event_id)
225	        if member is None or ev is None:
226	            continue
227	        if (ev.event_type or "").lower() in _POST_DEATH_EVENT_TYPES:
228	            continue
229	        death = _year(member.date_of_death)
230	        ev_year = _year(ev.date)
231	        if death is None or ev_year is None:
232	            continue
233	        if ev_year > death:
234	            issues.append(
235	                {
236	                    "id": issue_id_for("event_after_death", [member.id, ev.id]),
237	                    "issue_type": "event_after_death",
238	                    "severity": "warning",
239	                    "member_ids": [member.id],

172	def _sync_bridge_person(
173	    db: Session, member: Member, changes: dict, user: User
174	) -> tuple[str | None, Tree | None]:
175	    """Mirror identity-field edits onto the counterpart row of a bridge person.
176	
177	    The two rows represent the same human, so person-level facts edited on one
178	    side propagate to the other — but only while the tree_links feature is
179	    enabled and the actor may write the counterpart's tree; otherwise the rows
180	    simply drift until edited from a side with access.
181	
182	    Returns ``(status, counterpart_tree)``: ``("synced", tree)`` when the
183	    counterpart was updated, ``("skipped_no_access", None)`` when identity
184	    fields changed but the actor may not write the other tree (the one case
185	    the editor should be told about), and ``(None, None)`` when there was
186	    nothing to sync (no link, no identity change, feature off, counterpart
187	    gone).
188	    """
189	    if member.linked_member_id is None:
190	        return None, None
191	    synced = {k: v for k, v in changes.items() if k in BRIDGE_SYNC_FIELDS}
192	    if not synced:
193	        return None, None
194	    from app.services import feature_service  # noqa: PLC0415
195	
196	    if not feature_service.is_enabled(db, "tree_links", user):
197	        return None, None
198	    counterpart = db.get(Member, member.linked_member_id)
199	    if counterpart is None:
200	        return None, None
201	    target_tree = db.get(Tree, counterpart.tree_id)
202	    if target_tree is None:
203	        return None, None
204	    if not user.is_admin and role_for(db, target_tree, user) not in (
205	        "owner",
206	        "editor",
207	    ):
208	        return "skipped_no_access", None
209	    for key, value in synced.items():
210	        if key == "image_data" and value:
211	            # Media files are tree-scoped: copy the file into the
212	            # counterpart's tree instead of sharing the URL across trees.
213	            value = copy_media_to_tree(value, counterpart.tree_id)
214	        setattr(counterpart, key, value)
215	    return "synced", target_tree

531	def _sync_parent_slots(
532	    db: Session,
533	    tree: Tree,
534	    member: Member,
535	    paternal_changed: bool,
536	    paternal_parent_id: str | None,
537	    maternal_changed: bool,
538	    maternal_parent_id: str | None,
539	) -> None:
540	    """Apply explicit parent-slot changes without touching extra parent rows.
541	
542	    The persisted relation model has no slot column.  We reconstruct the two
543	    slots with the same gender-first rule as the frontend, then replace only a
544	    slot the request explicitly changed.  Replaying the same payload is a
545	    no-op, which keeps retries idempotent.
546	    """
547	    relations = list(
548	        db.scalars(
549	            select(Relation).where(
550	                Relation.tree_id == tree.id,
551	                Relation.from_member_id == member.id,
552	                Relation.relation_type == "parent",
553	            )
554	        ).all()
555	    )
556	    parent_ids = [relation.to_member_id for relation in relations]
557	    parents = {
558	        parent.id: parent
559	        for parent in db.scalars(
560	            select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree.id, Member.id.in_(parent_ids))
561	        ).all()
562	    }
563	
564	    paternal_current: str | None = None
565	    maternal_current: str | None = None
566	    for parent_id in parent_ids:
567	        gender = parents.get(parent_id).gender if parent_id in parents else None
568	        if gender == "m" and paternal_current is None:
569	            paternal_current = parent_id
570	        elif gender == "f" and maternal_current is None:
571	            maternal_current = parent_id
572	    for parent_id in parent_ids:
573	        if parent_id in {paternal_current, maternal_current}:
574	            continue
575	        if paternal_current is None:
576	            paternal_current = parent_id
577	        elif maternal_current is None:
578	            maternal_current = parent_id
579	
580	    for changed, previous, replacement in (
581	        (paternal_changed, paternal_current, paternal_parent_id),
582	        (maternal_changed, maternal_current, maternal_parent_id),
583	    ):
584	        if not changed:
585	            continue
586	        if replacement == previous:
587	            continue
588	        if previous is not None:
589	            relation = db.get(Relation, (tree.id, member.id, previous, "parent"))
590	            if relation is not None:
591	                db.delete(relation)

618	    db: Session,
619	    tree: Tree,
620	    member: Member,
621	    event_type: str,
622	    date: str | None,
623	    location: str | None,
624	) -> None:
625	    """Keep one member's birth/death event aligned without losing documents."""
626	    events = list(
627	        db.scalars(
628	            select(Event)
629	            .join(EventMemberLink, EventMemberLink.event_id == Event.id)
630	            .where(
631	                Event.tree_id == tree.id,
632	                Event.event_type == event_type,
633	                EventMemberLink.member_id == member.id,
634	            )
635	            .order_by(Event.id)
636	        ).all()
637	    )
638	    existing = events[0] if events else None
639	    if date:
640	        if existing is not None:
641	            # Do not replace the row: its description and linked documents
642	            # are user-authored details preserved by #659. The location is
643	            # only backfilled while still empty, so an existing (possibly
644	            # user-authored) location is never silently overwritten (#769).
645	            existing.date = date
646	            if location and not existing.location:
647	                existing.location = location
648	            return
649	        event = Event(
650	            id=str(uuid4()),
651	            tree_id=tree.id,
652	            event_type=event_type,

654	            location=location,
655	            created_at=utcnow_iso(),
656	        )

658	        db.flush()
659	        db.add(EventMemberLink(event_id=event.id, member_id=member.id))

664	@router.patch("/members/{member_id}", response_model=MemberOut)
665	def update_member(
666	    member_id: str,
667	    payload: MemberUpdate,
668	    tree: Tree = Depends(get_writable_tree),
669	    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
670	    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
671	):
672	    member = _get_member(db, tree, member_id)
673	    changes = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
674	    paternal_changed = "paternal_parent_id" in changes
675	    maternal_changed = "maternal_parent_id" in changes
676	    paternal_parent_id = changes.pop("paternal_parent_id", None)
677	    maternal_parent_id = changes.pop("maternal_parent_id", None)
678	    # The member form re-sends the link fields unchanged on every save. Only an
679	    # actual change is a link edit — an unchanged value must not re-run the
680	    # feature/access checks, otherwise ordinary edits fail once the tree_links
681	    # flag is turned off (or for editors without access to the linked tree).
682	    if "linked_tree_id" in changes and changes["linked_tree_id"] == member.linked_tree_id:
683	        del changes["linked_tree_id"]
684	    if (
685	        "linked_member_id" in changes
686	        and changes["linked_member_id"] == member.linked_member_id
687	    ):
688	        del changes["linked_member_id"]
689	    unlinked_counterpart_tree: Tree | None = None
690	    if "linked_tree_id" in changes:
691	        if changes["linked_tree_id"] is not None:
692	            # Establishing a link requires resolving a bridge person on both
693	            # sides, which touches two trees — this single-row endpoint can't
694	            # do that safely. Only clearing (null) or leaving it unchanged is
695	            # allowed here; see POST /members/{id}/link.
696	            raise HTTPException(
697	                status_code=400,
698	                detail="Establish tree links via the link endpoint",
699	            )
700	        _validate_linked_tree(db, tree, user, changes["linked_tree_id"])
701	        # Unlinking invalidates the counterpart pointer into the old tree.
702	        changes["linked_member_id"] = None
703	        # Tear down the other side too: a bridge is symmetric, so unlinking
704	        # here must also clear the counterpart's fields. Otherwise the link
705	        # lingers in the other tree (phantom badge) and identity edits keep
706	        # flowing one-directionally from the still-linked counterpart back to
707	        # this member. Cleared unconditionally, like the delete path — this is
708	        # integrity cleanup of a now-broken bridge, not a content edit.
709	        if member.linked_member_id is not None:
710	            counterpart = db.get(Member, member.linked_member_id)
711	            if counterpart is not None:
712	                counterpart.linked_tree_id = None
713	                counterpart.linked_member_id = None
714	                unlinked_counterpart_tree = db.get(Tree, counterpart.tree_id)
715	    if changes.get("linked_member_id") is not None:
716	        _validate_linked_member(
717	            db,
718	            changes.get("linked_tree_id", member.linked_tree_id),
719	            changes["linked_member_id"],
720	            member.id,
721	        )
722	    new_image_url: str | None = None
723	    if "image_data" in changes:
724	        try:
725	            new_url = process_image_field(
726	                tree.id,
727	                changes["image_data"],
728	                get_media_limits(db),
729	            )
730	            changes["image_data"] = new_url
731	            if new_url and new_url.startswith(MEDIA_URL_PREFIX):
732	                new_image_url = new_url
733	        except ImageTooLarge as exc:
734	            raise HTTPException(status_code=413, detail=str(exc)) from exc
735	        except (UnsupportedImageType, ValueError) as exc:
736	            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(exc)) from exc
737	
738	    # Check media quota for the new image (write-then-verify: file already on
739	    # disk and counted by compute_usage, so pass 0 to avoid double-counting).
740	    if new_image_url:
741	        try:
742	            check_media_quota(db, tree, 0)
743	        except QuotaExceeded as exc:
744	            delete_media(new_image_url)
745	            raise HTTPException(status_code=413, detail=str(exc)) from exc
746	    # Capture before-state for diff details (skip noisy positional/internal fields).
747	    _SKIP_DIFF = {"position_x", "position_y", "is_collapsed", "image_data"}
748	    before = {k: getattr(member, k) for k in changes if k not in _SKIP_DIFF}
749	    for key, value in changes.items():
750	        setattr(member, key, value)
751	    if paternal_changed or maternal_changed:
752	        _sync_parent_slots(
753	            db,
754	            tree,
755	            member,
756	            paternal_changed,
757	            paternal_parent_id,
758	            maternal_changed,
759	            maternal_parent_id,
760	        )
761	    vital_events_changed = _event_updates_allowed(db, tree, user) and (
762	        "date_of_birth" in changes
763	        or "date_of_death" in changes
764	        or "birthplace" in changes
765	        or "cemetery" in changes
766	    )
767	    if vital_events_changed:
768	        # member fields above are already mutated by the setattr loop, so the
769	        # current date/place reflect this save even when only one of the pair
770	        # (e.g. birthplace without a date change) was actually sent.
771	        if "date_of_birth" in changes or "birthplace" in changes:
772	            _sync_vital_event(
773	                db, tree, member, "birth", member.date_of_birth, member.birthplace
774	            )
775	        if "date_of_death" in changes or "cemetery" in changes:
776	            _sync_vital_event(
777	                db, tree, member, "death", member.date_of_death, member.cemetery
778	            )
779	    after = {k: getattr(member, k) for k in before}
780	    # Bridge person: mirror identity edits onto the counterpart row so the
781	    # same human stays consistent on both sides of a tree-in-tree link.
782	    bridge_sync, synced_tree = _sync_bridge_person(db, member, changes, user)
783	    diff_details: dict | None = None
784	    changed = {
785	        k: {"before": before[k], "after": after[k]}
786	        for k in before
787	        if before[k] != after[k]
788	    }
789	    if changed:
790	        diff_details = {
791	            "before": {k: v["before"] for k, v in changed.items()},
792	            "after": {k: v["after"] for k, v in changed.items()},
793	        }
794	    label = " ".join(filter(None, [member.first_name, member.last_name])) or None
795	    record_activity(
796	        db,
797	        tree_id=tree.id,
798	        actor=user,
799	        action="update",
800	        target_type="member",
801	        target_id=member.id,
802	        target_label=label,
803	        details=diff_details,
804	    )
805	    db.commit()
806	    publish_tree_event(db, tree, "activity.entry_added", {"tree_id": tree.id})
807	    db.refresh(member)
808	    publish_tree_event(
809	        db,
810	        tree,
811	        "tree.content_changed",
812	        {"tree_id": tree.id, "domain": "member"},
813	    )
814	    if vital_events_changed:
815	        publish_tree_event(
816	            db,
817	            tree,
818	            "tree.content_changed",
819	            {"tree_id": tree.id, "domain": "event"},
820	        )
821	    invalidate_stats(tree.id)
822	    if synced_tree is not None:
823	        publish_tree_event(
824	            db,
825	            synced_tree,
826	            "tree.content_changed",
827	            {"tree_id": synced_tree.id, "domain": "member"},
828	        )
829	        invalidate_stats(synced_tree.id)
830	    if unlinked_counterpart_tree is not None:
831	        publish_tree_event(
832	            db,
833	            unlinked_counterpart_tree,
834	            "tree.content_changed",
835	            {"tree_id": unlinked_counterpart_tree.id, "domain": "member"},
836	        )
837	        invalidate_stats(unlinked_counterpart_tree.id)
838	    out = MemberOut.model_validate(member)
839	    out.bridge_sync = bridge_sync
840	    return out

882	@router.get(
883	    "/members/{member_id}/link-candidates",
884	    response_model=LinkCandidatesOut,
885	)
886	def get_link_candidates(
887	    member_id: str,
888	    target_tree_id: str = Query(...),
889	    tree: Tree = Depends(get_writable_tree),
890	    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
891	    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
892	):
893	    """List same-named members of ``target_tree_id`` that could be the bridge
894	    counterpart for ``member_id`` — i.e. candidates for ``POST .../link``
895	    with ``mode="existing"``.
896	
897	    Only members matching the source member's name+gender key are returned
898	    (a bridge person is the same human on both sides, so an unrelated match
899	    would be meaningless), excluding the source member itself and anyone
900	    already linked to another tree. Each candidate is shaped as a
901	    ``DuplicatePair`` (reusing the tree-merge machinery) so the client can
902	    render the same conflict-resolution UI merge already uses.
903	    """
904	    from app.services import feature_service  # noqa: PLC0415
905	    from app.services.merge import (  # noqa: PLC0415
906	        compute_conflicts,
907	        member_key,
908	        member_name_key,
909	    )
910	
911	    if not feature_service.is_enabled(db, "tree_links", user):
912	        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Not found")
913	    member = _get_member(db, tree, member_id)
914	
915	    _validate_linked_tree(db, tree, user, target_tree_id)
916	    target = db.get(Tree, target_tree_id)
917	    if target is None:
918	        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Linked tree not found")
919	    # Candidates are only useful if the caller can actually link one, which
920	    # requires write access to the target (same check the link endpoint uses).
921	    if not user.is_admin and role_for(db, target, user) not in ("owner", "editor"):
922	        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="No write access to the linked tree")
923	
924	    source_name_key = member_name_key(member)
925	    source_exact_key = member_key(member)
926	    candidates: list[DuplicatePair] = []
927	    for candidate in db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == target.id)):
928	        if candidate.id == member.id:
929	            continue
930	        if candidate.linked_tree_id is not None:
931	            continue
932	        if member_name_key(candidate) != source_name_key:
933	            continue
934	        match = "exact" if member_key(candidate) == source_exact_key else "possible"
935	        candidates.append(
936	            DuplicatePair(
937	                member_a=MemberOut.model_validate(member),
938	                member_b=MemberOut.model_validate(candidate),
939	                match=match,
940	                conflicts=compute_conflicts(member, candidate),
941	                default_action="merge",
942	            )
943	        )
944	    return LinkCandidatesOut(candidates=candidates)

947	@router.post(
948	    "/members/{member_id}/link",
949	    response_model=MemberSubtreeOut,
950	    status_code=201,
951	)
952	def link_member_to_tree(
953	    member_id: str,
954	    payload: MemberLinkRequest,
955	    tree: Tree = Depends(get_writable_tree),
956	    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
957	    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
958	):
959	    """Establish a tree-in-tree bridge between this member and a target tree.
960	
961	    Unlike ``PATCH /members/{id}`` (which can only clear a link, never create
962	    one — see the loophole this closes), this endpoint always resolves a real
963	    bridge person on both sides: either an existing member the caller asserts
964	    is the same person (``mode="existing"``), or a fresh clone seeded into the
965	    target tree (``mode="create"``). Establishing a link writes rows in two
966	    trees, so it requires write access to both.
967	    """
968	    from app.services import feature_service  # noqa: PLC0415
969	    from app.services.merge import _clone_member, _wire_bridge  # noqa: PLC0415
970	
971	    if not feature_service.is_enabled(db, "tree_links", user):
972	        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Not found")
973	    member = _get_member(db, tree, member_id)
974	    if member.linked_tree_id is not None:
975	        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="Member is already linked to a tree")
976	
977	    _validate_linked_tree(db, tree, user, payload.linked_tree_id)
978	    target = db.get(Tree, payload.linked_tree_id)
979	    if target is None:
980	        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Linked tree not found")
981	    # Establishing a bridge writes the counterpart row too, so read access to
982	    # the target (already checked by _validate_linked_tree) is not enough.
983	    if not user.is_admin and role_for(db, target, user) not in ("owner", "editor"):
984	        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="No write access to the linked tree")
985	
986	    if payload.mode == "create":
987	        counterpart = _clone_member(member, target.id, str(uuid4()))
988	        counterpart.position_x = 0
989	        counterpart.position_y = 0
990	        counterpart.is_collapsed = False
991	        db.add(counterpart)
992	        db.flush()
993	    else:
994	        if payload.counterpart_member_id is None:
995	            raise HTTPException(
996	                status_code=400,
997	                detail="counterpart_member_id is required for mode=existing",
998	            )
999	        counterpart = db.get(Member, payload.counterpart_member_id)
1000	        if counterpart is None or counterpart.tree_id != target.id:
1001	            raise HTTPException(
1002	                status_code=400,
1003	                detail="Counterpart member is not part of the linked tree",
1004	            )
1005	        if counterpart.id == member.id:
1006	            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="A member cannot link to itself")
1007	        if counterpart.linked_tree_id is not None:
1008	            raise HTTPException(
1009	                status_code=400,
1010	                detail="Counterpart member is already linked to a tree",
1011	            )
1012	
1013	    _wire_bridge(member, counterpart)
1014	    if payload.mode == "existing":
1015	        # The two rows may describe the same person with differing details
1016	        # (dates, places, notes, ...) — reconcile them onto both sides now
1017	        # rather than letting the bridge start out of sync. field_choices is
1018	        # ignored for mode="create": the counterpart there is a fresh clone of
1019	        # `member`, so there is nothing to reconcile.
1020	        from app.services.merge import reconcile_bridge_fields  # noqa: PLC0415
1021	
1022	        reconcile_bridge_fields(member, counterpart, payload.field_choices)
1023	
1024	    label = " ".join(filter(None, [member.first_name, member.last_name])) or None
1025	    record_activity(
1026	        db,
1027	        tree_id=tree.id,
1028	        actor=user,
1029	        action="update",
1030	        target_type="member",
1031	        target_id=member.id,
1032	        target_label=label,
1033	        details={"after": {"linked_tree_id": target.id}},
1034	    )
1035	    counterpart_label = (
1036	        " ".join(filter(None, [counterpart.first_name, counterpart.last_name])) or None
1037	    )
1038	    if payload.mode == "create":
1039	        record_activity(
1040	            db,
1041	            tree_id=target.id,
1042	            actor=user,
1043	            action="create",
1044	            target_type="member",
1045	            target_id=counterpart.id,
1046	            target_label=counterpart_label,
1047	        )
1048	    else:
1049	        record_activity(
1050	            db,
1051	            tree_id=target.id,
1052	            actor=user,
1053	            action="update",
1054	            target_type="member",
1055	            target_id=counterpart.id,
1056	            target_label=counterpart_label,
1057	            details={"after": {"linked_tree_id": tree.id}},
1058	        )
1059	    db.commit()
1060	    publish_tree_event(db, tree, "activity.entry_added", {"tree_id": tree.id})
1061	    publish_tree_event(db, target, "activity.entry_added", {"tree_id": target.id})
1062	    db.refresh(member)
1063	    db.refresh(target)
1064	    publish_tree_event(
1065	        db,
1066	        tree,
1067	        "tree.content_changed",
1068	        {"tree_id": tree.id, "domain": "member"},
1069	    )
1070	    invalidate_stats(tree.id)
1071	    publish_tree_event(
1072	        db,
1073	        target,
1074	        "tree.content_changed",
1075	        {"tree_id": target.id, "domain": "member"},
1076	    )
1077	    invalidate_stats(target.id)
1078	    return MemberSubtreeOut(
1079	        tree=TreeOut.model_validate(target),
1080	        anchor=MemberOut.model_validate(member),
1081	    )

1117	    )

1119

31	def _bridge_drift_issues(
32	    db: Session, user: User, members: list[Member]
33	) -> list[dict]:
34	    """Bridge persons whose two rows have drifted apart.
35	
36	    Needs the db (counterpart rows live in other trees), so it runs here
37	    rather than in the pure ``run_quality_checks``. The comparison happens
38	    server-side only — field *names* are reported, never the other tree's
39	    values — and the whole check is dormant while tree_links is off.
40	    """
41	    linked = [m for m in members if m.linked_member_id]
42	    if not linked:
43	        return []
44	    from app.services import feature_service  # noqa: PLC0415
45	
46	    if not feature_service.is_enabled(db, "tree_links", user):
47	        return []
48	    counterparts = {
49	        c.id: c
50	        for c in db.scalars(
51	            select(Member).where(
52	                Member.id.in_([m.linked_member_id for m in linked])
53	            )
54	        )
55	    }
56	    issues: list[dict] = []
57	    for m in linked:
58	        counterpart = counterparts.get(m.linked_member_id)
59	        if counterpart is None:
60	            continue
61	        fields = drift_fields(m, counterpart)
62	        if not fields:
63	            continue
64	        issues.append(
65	            {
66	                # Hash the drifted field set too, so a dismissed note comes
67	                # back when *new* fields start to differ.
68	                "id": issue_id_for("bridge_person_drift", [m.id, *fields]),
69	                "issue_type": "bridge_person_drift",
70	                "severity": "warning",
71	                "member_ids": [m.id],
72	                "description": (
73	                    "Differs from the linked copy in another tree: "
74	                    f"{', '.join(f.replace('_', ' ') for f in fields)}."
75	                ),
76	            }
77	        )
78	    return issues
79

81	@router.get("/quality-report", response_model=QualityReport)
82	def get_quality_report(
83	    include_dismissed: bool = False,
84	    tree: Tree = Depends(get_readable_tree),
85	    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
86	    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
87	):
88	    """Return a non-destructive data-quality report for the tree.
89	
90	    Accessible to anyone with at least read access. Dismissed issues are
91	    excluded by default; pass ``include_dismissed=true`` to get the full
92	    list with each issue's ``dismissed`` flag set.
93	    """
94	    members = list(db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree.id)).all())
95	    relations = list(
96	        db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == tree.id)).all()
97	    )
98	    events = list(db.scalars(select(Event).where(Event.tree_id == tree.id)).all())
99	    event_links = list(
100	        db.scalars(
101	            select(EventMemberLink)
102	            .join(Event, Event.id == EventMemberLink.event_id)
103	            .where(Event.tree_id == tree.id)
104	        ).all()
105	    )
106	    raw_issues = run_quality_checks(members, relations, events, event_links)
107	    raw_issues += _bridge_drift_issues(db, user, members)
108	
109	    dismissed_ids = set(
110	        db.scalars(
111	            select(QualityIssueDismissal.issue_id).where(
112	                QualityIssueDismissal.tree_id == tree.id
113	            )
114	        ).all()
115	    )
116	
117	    issues = [QualityIssue(**i, dismissed=i["id"] in dismissed_ids) for i in raw_issues]
118	    if not include_dismissed:
119	        issues = [i for i in issues if not i.dismissed]
120	
121	    return QualityReport(
122	        tree_id=tree.id,
123	        total_members=len(members),
124	        issues=issues,
125	    )

15	
16	The helper only calls ``db.add(...)``; it does NOT commit so the new row
17	participates in the route's own transaction and is rolled back on error.
18	"""
19	
20	import json
21	
22	from sqlalchemy import inspect, or_, select
23	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
24	
25	from app.db.base import Base
26	from app.models.activity import ActivityLog
27	from app.models.content import (
28	    DocumentMemberLink,
29	    EventMemberLink,
30	    GalleryMemberLink,
31	    MemberTaskLink,
32	    StoryMemberLink,
33	)

36	
37	# Version of the delete-snapshot payload shape stored in ``details``
38	# (see docs/ACTIVITY_AUDIT.md §b). Bump when the shape changes so a future
39	# undo feature can dispatch on it.
40	SNAPSHOT_VERSION = 1
41	
42	
43	def row_to_dict(obj: Base) -> dict:
44	    """Serialize a mapped row's column values into a JSON-safe dict.
45	
46	    Uses mapper inspection so columns added by future migrations are picked up
47	    automatically. All column types in the snapshotted tables are str / float /
48	    bool / None, which ``json.dumps`` handles directly.
49	    """
50	    return {attr.key: getattr(obj, attr.key) for attr in inspect(obj).mapper.column_attrs}
51	
52	
53	def delete_snapshot(**tables: object) -> dict:
54	    """Wrap per-table pre-image data into the versioned delete payload."""
55	    return {"snapshot": {"version": SNAPSHOT_VERSION, **tables}}
56	
57	
58	def member_delete_snapshot(
59	    db: Session, member: Member, counterpart: Member | None = None
60	) -> dict:
61	    """Full pre-image of a member row and its cascade children.
62	
63	    Must be called BEFORE ``db.delete(member)``. Captures everything the DB
64	    cascade will remove: relations on either side, disease records, and the
65	    five content link tables (research-task rows themselves survive a member
66	    delete; only their links cascade). ``counterpart`` is the bridge person in the
67	    linked tree whose link pointers the delete route dissolves; its identity
68	    is recorded so the tree-in-tree link can be re-established on undo.
69	    Virtual-view match rows also cascade but are derived state the matching
70	    service recomputes, so they are deliberately not snapshotted.
71	    """
72	    relations = db.scalars(
73	        select(Relation).where(
74	            or_(
75	                Relation.from_member_id == member.id,
76	                Relation.to_member_id == member.id,
77	            )
78	        )
79	    ).all()
80	    diseases = db.scalars(
81	        select(MemberDisease).where(MemberDisease.member_id == member.id)
82	    ).all()
83	    tables: dict[str, object] = {
84	        "member": row_to_dict(member),
85	        "relations": [row_to_dict(r) for r in relations],
86	        "diseases": [row_to_dict(d) for d in diseases],
87	    }
88	    for key, model in (
89	        ("task_links", MemberTaskLink),
90	        ("event_links", EventMemberLink),
91	        ("story_links", StoryMemberLink),
92	        ("gallery_links", GalleryMemberLink),
93	        ("document_links", DocumentMemberLink),
94	    ):
95	        rows = db.scalars(select(model).where(model.member_id == member.id)).all()
96	        tables[key] = [row_to_dict(r) for r in rows]
97	    if counterpart is not None:
98	        tables["bridge"] = {
99	            "counterpart_member_id": counterpart.id,
100	            "counterpart_tree_id": counterpart.tree_id,
101	        }
102	    return delete_snapshot(**tables)
103	
104

50	/**

52	 * `default_action` suggestion and its conflict list.
53	 */
54	export function buildInitialResolutionState(
55	  pair: DuplicatePair,
56	): PairResolutionState {
57	  const fields: Partial<Record<string, MergeFieldChoice>> = {};
58	  for (const field of pair.conflicts) {
59	    // Default field choice: "a" (keep source-A value)
60	    fields[field] = "a";
61	  }
62	  return {
63	    action: pair.default_action,
64	    fields,
65	  };
66	}

70	 * by POST /trees/merge.

72	 * Only pairs that are not using the server default need a resolution entry,
73	 * but we send all to keep the logic simple.
74	 */
75	export function buildResolutionsPayload(
76	  pairs: DuplicatePair[],
77	  states: Map<string, PairResolutionState>,
78	): MergeResolution[] {
79	  return pairs.map((pair) => {
80	    const pairKey = buildPairKey(pair.member_a.id, pair.member_b.id);
81	    const state = states.get(pairKey) ?? buildInitialResolutionState(pair);
82	    return {

86	      fields: state.action === "merge" ? { ...state.fields } : {},
87	    };

def test_preview_exact_duplicates(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    ta = make_tree(db, user, "A")
    tb = make_tree(db, user, "B")

    add_member(db, ta, "a1", first_name="Henry", last_name="Miller", gender="m",
               date_of_birth="1920", additional_data="Note A", birthplace="Berlin")
    add_member(db, tb, "b1", first_name="Henry", last_name="Miller", gender="m",
               date_of_birth="1920", additional_data="Note B", birthplace="Hamburg")

    preview = compute_merge_preview(db, user, ta.id, tb.id)

    assert preview.total_members == 2
    assert preview.merged_count == 1
    assert len(preview.duplicates) == 1
    pair = preview.duplicates[0]
    assert pair.match == "exact"
    assert pair.default_action == "merge"
    assert "additional_data" in pair.conflicts
    assert "birthplace" in pair.conflicts


def test_preview_possible_candidate(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    ta = make_tree(db, user, "A")
    tb = make_tree(db, user, "B")

    add_member(db, ta, "a1", first_name="Anna", last_name="Schmidt", gender="f",
               date_of_birth="1950")
    # Same name+gender but different birth date → possible
    add_member(db, tb, "b1", first_name="Anna", last_name="Schmidt", gender="f",
               date_of_birth="1951")

    preview = compute_merge_preview(db, user, ta.id, tb.id)

    assert preview.total_members == 2
    assert len(preview.duplicates) == 1
    pair = preview.duplicates[0]
    assert pair.match == "possible"

input.prompt:
We are implementing GitHub issue #729 in the family-tree repo (React+TS frontend, FastAPI+SQLAlchemy backend). Produce a detailed, concrete implementation plan (file-by-file, function-by-function where useful). Do NOT write code — this is a planning pass only. I will implement it myself afterward.

## Issue #729: Duplicate merge assistant — merge two members in place from the quality report

### Context already gathered (do not re-derive, just use it)

Two finished subsystems aren't connected yet:
- The quality report (`backend/app/services/quality_checks.py`) flags `duplicate_candidate` findings (members sharing the same full name — note: `member_ids` for this issue type can have MORE than 2 ids if 3+ members share a name), but the UI (`frontend/src/components/view/quality-report-view/QualityReportView.tsx`) only offers *dismiss*.
- `backend/app/services/merge.py` already has `compute_merge_preview`/`merge_trees` for TREE-level merges (merging two whole trees into a brand new third tree), with per-pair conflict detection (`compute_conflicts`, `CONFLICT_FIELDS`) and per-field resolution application (`apply_field_choices`). There's also `reconcile_bridge_fields` used by the tree-linking bridge-person flow, and `_clone_member`/`_wire_bridge` helpers. None of this writes in-place inside a single tree — it always clones into a new/different tree.

Goal: a guided IN-PLACE merge of two members of the SAME tree — pick a `keep_id` and a `remove_id`, resolve field conflicts, transfer all of remove's relations/content onto keep, then delete remove. Entry point launched from a `duplicate_candidate` finding in the quality report.

### Required backend work

1. **Preview endpoint** (new, e.g. `GET /trees/{tree_id}/members/{member_id}/merge-preview?with={other_member_id}` or similar — pick a clean REST shape) that returns field conflicts for the pair, reusing/extracting `compute_conflicts`/`CONFLICT_FIELDS` from `merge.py` rather than forking the logic. Should return something shaped like the existing `DuplicatePair` schema (`backend/app/schemas/merge.py`) so the frontend can reuse `MergeConflictResolver.tsx` (see below) with minimal changes — but this is a same-tree pair, not a cross-tree pair, so double check whether `DuplicatePair` as-is fits or needs a variant.
2. **`POST /trees/{tree_id}/members/merge`** taking `keep_id`, `remove_id`, and field resolutions (reuse `apply_field_choices`'s a/b/combine semantics and its `text_fields` combine set). Must, within one DB transaction:
   - Guard: both members must belong to `tree_id` (404 otherwise), refuse `keep_id == remove_id` (400), refuse if merging would create a relationship cycle — reuse the cycle-detection DFS logic in `run_quality_checks` (`backend/app/services/quality_checks.py`, section "3. Relationship cycles") rather than forking it; that logic currently operates on parent-only relation pairs built from `Relation` rows where `relation_type == "parent"` and `from_member_id` = child, `to_member_id` = parent. Think carefully about how a merge could create a cycle (e.g. remove_id is an ancestor of keep_id via a different path, or remove_id and keep_id are both parents of each other through different children) and how re-pointing relations changes the parent graph before you'd need to check it.
   - Union relations from both members onto `keep_id`: for every `Relation` row where `from_member_id == remove_id` or `to_member_id == remove_id`, repoint that column to `keep_id`; drop the row if after repointing it would be a self-relation (`from_member_id == to_member_id`) or a duplicate of a relation that already exists on `keep_id` (same `(from_member_id, to_member_id, relation_type)` triple after repointing, given `Relation`'s composite PK is exactly that triple — see `backend/app/models/family.py`).
   - Transfer content links: `EventMemberLink`, `StoryMemberLink`, `GalleryMemberLink`, `DocumentMemberLink`, `MemberTaskLink`, `MemberDisease` (all in `backend/app/models/content.py` / `family.py`) — repoint `member_id` from `remove_id` to `keep_id`; for the four link tables (composite PK of `(content_id, member_id)`), drop-on-duplicate the same way as relations. `MemberDisease` has its own `id` PK plus `member_id`/`name` — decide dedup policy (the tree-merge code dedupes diseases by `(member_id, normalized name)` — consider reusing that policy here too, or note if in-place merge should just keep both since it's a real content row, not a structural link — your call, state the reasoning).
   - `GalleryUnknownFace`/other tables don't reference `member_id` directly (check `backend/app/models/content.py` if unsure) — skip anything that isn't member-scoped.
   - Keep the chosen photo (`image_data` conflict field, `a`/`b`/`combine`-with-fallback-to-a per `apply_field_choices`'s existing semantics — note `image_data` isn't in `apply_field_choices`'s `text_fields` combine set, so "combine" isn't a valid choice for it; decide what to do if the frontend sends combine for image_data anyway — probably just don't offer it in the UI).
   - Combine notes/`additional_data` per the existing `combine` semantics.
   - Bridge-person link fields (`linked_tree_id`/`linked_member_id`) on the removed member: decide what happens if the member being removed is itself a bridge person (has a linked counterpart in another tree) — probably the safest behavior is to carry the link onto `keep_id` if `keep_id` has no link of its own, otherwise leave `remove_id`'s link to be silently dropped, OR refuse the merge if both are separately linked. State your recommendation.
   - Physically delete the `remove_id` `Member` row at the end (after re-pointing everything so the delete doesn't cascade away content that should have survived — check FK `ondelete` behavior on `Relation`/link tables, they're all `CASCADE` on `member_id`, so anything not explicitly re-pointed before the delete is lost).
   - `record_activity(...)` with a rich payload — look at `member_delete_snapshot()` in `backend/app/services/activity.py` (used by the existing single-member delete route) for the existing full pre-image snapshot shape/pattern (version-tagged `{"snapshot": {"version":.., ...}}"`), and produce something structurally similar/reusable for the merge case per the issue's note about aligning with #572 (reversibility) — you don't need to implement undo, just produce a payload rich enough that a future undo feature could use it (full pre-image of the removed member + its relations/links/diseases, similar to `member_delete_snapshot`, plus whatever pre-image is needed of the KEPT member's conflicting fields before they were overwritten by resolution choices).
   - Fire the same `publish_tree_event(..., "tree.content_changed", {"domain": "member"})` / `invalidate_stats` side effects that `update_member`/`delete_member` in `backend/app/api/routes/members.py` already do, so the frontend's live-update wiring picks it up the same way.
3. Where should these two endpoints live? `backend/app/api/routes/members.py` (member CRUD, uses `get_writable_tree`) seems like the natural home per the issue ("the endpoint itself is core member CRUD, not separately flagged") — confirm and specify exact route paths, request/response Pydantic schemas (where they go — `backend/app/schemas/merge.py` has the existing merge-related schemas; decide if new same-tree-merge schemas belong there or in `backend/app/schemas/family.py`).
4. Backend tests: specify what new test file(s) (e.g. `backend/tests/test_member_merge.py`) and what cases — relation re-pointing (including a case that currently would create a duplicate relation and must be dropped, not integrity-error), link transfer for each of the 5-6 link tables, guard rails (self-merge, cross-tree members, cycle creation), activity log payload shape, and the preview endpoint's conflict output. Look at `backend/tests/test_merge_preview.py` and `backend/tests/conftest.py` (`add_member`, `make_tree`, `make_user`, `share` helpers) for existing conventions to follow.

### Required frontend work

1. **"Merge…" action** on `duplicate_candidate` findings in `frontend/src/components/view/quality-report-view/QualityReportView.tsx`'s `IssueCard` component (parallel to the existing `isBridgeDrift` push/pull buttons pattern at the bottom of that component). Since `duplicate_candidate.member_ids` can list MORE than 2 members (3+ people sharing a name), the UI needs to let the user pick which 2 of the N to merge if N > 2 (simplest: if exactly 2, go straight to the dialog with those two; if more, show a small picker first, or default to first two with a select — your call, keep it simple and state the choice).
2. **Merge dialog**: side-by-side field comparison + per-field pick, shaped like `frontend/src/components/view/database-management-view/dialog/MergeConflictResolver.tsx` (already reused as-is by `frontend/src/components/shared/member-sheet/LinkExistingTreeDialog.tsx` for the tree-linking flow — same reuse pattern should apply here), plus a preview section showing counts of what will be transferred (relations/events/stories/gallery items/documents/tasks/diseases) before confirming. Decide: does this need a NEW dialog component (e.g. `MergeMembersDialog.tsx`) that wraps `MergeConflictResolver` + a "keep which member as primary" chooser + the transfer-preview list + confirm button, likely living next to `QualityReportView.tsx` or in `frontend/src/components/shared/member-sheet/`? Specify exact location and prop shape.
3. Reuse `frontend/src/utils/mergeUtils.ts` (`PairResolutionState`, `buildInitialResolutionState`, `RESOLVABLE_FIELDS`, `COMBINABLE_FIELDS`) as much as possible — note `RESOLVABLE_FIELDS` currently includes `imageData` but that's NOT in `COMBINABLE_FIELDS`, consistent with the backend gap above.
4. New `TreeService` methods (pattern in `frontend/src/services/TreeService.ts`, e.g. near `getLinkCandidates`/`resolveBridgeDrift`/`getQualityReport`) for the preview and merge endpoints, and new types in `frontend/src/types/merge.ts` if the response shape differs from `DuplicatePair`.
5. New store action — decide whether this belongs in `useMemberStore.ts` (has `removeMember`/`updateMemberPartial` patterns, undo-grace-period machinery for delete — note a merge is NOT the same as a plain delete-with-undo, so don't necessarily reuse that specific undo mechanism) or `useQualityReportStore.ts` (has `refreshReport`/`resolveBridgeDrift` patterns) — likely needs to refresh both the quality report AND the member list afterward. Specify exact function signature and what it calls/refreshes.
6. i18n: this repo has only TWO locales, `frontend/src/i18n/locales/en.json` and `de.json` — both must get new keys (English content required, plus give the German translations too since I'll need them). New keys likely needed under `quality-report-view` (a "Merge…" button/action + any picker-of-2 copy) and either a new top-level namespace (e.g. `merge-members-dialog`) or nested under `merge-view` for the dialog itself — specify exact key paths and English strings (I'll translate to German separately or you can also supply German).
7. Note CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md governs: TypeScript strict (no `any`), all user-facing text via i18next in every locale, `npm run check-i18n` must pass, layout is recomputed via `frontend/src/utils/layoutUtils.ts` (dagre) — never set node positions manually — after a merge changes tree structure, how should the layout recompute be triggered? Look at how other structural changes (e.g. `removeMember`, `addRelation`) end up triggering a layout recompute today (check `frontend/src/hooks/memberStoreLayout.ts` and how `refreshMembers`/`tree.content_changed` websocket events interact with layout) and specify what the merge action needs to call.

### Deliverable

A step-by-step plan covering: exact new files, exact modified files with what changes in each, exact new route paths + Pydantic schema shapes, the relation/link re-pointing algorithm in enough detail to implement directly, the cycle-guard algorithm, the activity-log payload shape, the frontend component tree and prop shapes, the i18n keys (English + German), and the test files/cases to add on both sides. Flag any open design decisions you had to make a judgment call on (dedup policy for diseases, bridge-link handling, picker-of-2 UI, undo-mechanism reuse) so I can sanity check them before implementation starts.

35	    """Deterministic id for an issue, derived from its type and members.
36	
37	    Issues are recomputed fresh on every request rather than stored, so this

39	    underlying data produces the same issue, it hashes to the same id.

"""In-place, same-tree member merge (#729).

Unlike ``app.services.merge`` (which clones two whole *trees* into a brand
new third tree), this combines two *members of the same tree*: one survives
(``keep``), the other is removed (``remove``) after everything it owns —
relations, content links, diseases, and an optional tree-in-tree bridge — has
been re-pointed onto ``keep``. Field-conflict detection/resolution is reused
from ``app.services.merge`` rather than forked.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from types import SimpleNamespace

from fastapi import HTTPException
from pydantic.alias_generators import to_camel
from sqlalchemy import func, or_, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.models import (
    DocumentMemberLink,
    EventMemberLink,
    GalleryMemberLink,
    Member,
    MemberDisease,
    MemberTaskLink,
    Relation,
    StoryMemberLink,
    Tree,
    User,
)
from app.schemas.family import MemberOut
from app.schemas.merge import (
    DuplicatePair,
    MemberMergePreviewOut,
    MemberMergeTransferCounts,
)
from app.services.activity import SNAPSHOT_VERSION, member_delete_snapshot
from app.services.merge import (
    CONFLICT_FIELDS,
    _norm,
    _to_snake_case,
    apply_field_choices,
    compute_conflicts,
    member_key,
)
from app.services.quality_checks import find_parent_cycle_members


def compute_member_merge_preview(
    db: Session, tree: Tree, keep: Member, remove: Member
) -> MemberMergePreviewOut:
    """Field conflicts plus counts of what a merge would transfer onto ``keep``.

    Conflicts are reported in camelCase (unlike the tree-merge preview, whose
    ``conflicts`` are the raw snake_case attribute names) so the response
    lines up with the frontend's ``RESOLVABLE_FIELDS``/``MergeConflictResolver``
    without a translation layer on the client.
    """
    conflicts = [to_camel(field) for field in compute_conflicts(keep, remove)]
    match = "exact" if member_key(keep) == member_key(remove) else "possible"
    pair = DuplicatePair(
        member_a=MemberOut.model_validate(keep),
        member_b=MemberOut.model_validate(remove),
        match=match,
        conflicts=conflicts,
        default_action="merge",
    )

    def _count(model: type, column) -> int:
        return db.scalar(select(func.count()).where(column == remove.id)) or 0

    relations = (
        db.scalar(
            select(func.count())
            .select_from(Relation)
            .where(
                Relation.tree_id == tree.id,
                or_(
                    Relation.from_member_id == remove.id,
                    Relation.to_member_id == remove.id,
                ),
            )
        )
        or 0
    )

    transfer = MemberMergeTransferCounts(
        relations=relations,
        events=_count(EventMemberLink, EventMemberLink.member_id),
        stories=_count(StoryMemberLink, StoryMemberLink.member_id),
        gallery=_count(GalleryMemberLink, GalleryMemberLink.member_id),
        documents=_count(DocumentMemberLink, DocumentMemberLink.member_id),
        tasks=_count(MemberTaskLink, MemberTaskLink.member_id),
        diseases=_count(MemberDisease, MemberDisease.member_id),
    )
    return MemberMergePreviewOut(pair=pair, transfer=transfer)


def _repoint_member_links(
    db: Session,
    model: type,
    id_field: str,
    keep_id: str,
    remove_id: str,
    extra_fields: tuple[str, ...] = (),
) -> None:
    """Union a member-link table onto ``keep_id``, dropping duplicates.

    Every content link table (events, stories, gallery, documents, tasks) has
    the same composite-PK shape: ``(<content>_id, member_id)``. A link already
    on ``keep_id`` wins; ``remove_id``'s copy is simply dropped rather than
    causing a primary-key clash.
    """
    keep_ids = {
        getattr(row, id_field)
        for row in db.scalars(select(model).where(model.member_id == keep_id))
    }
    to_add: list[dict] = []
    for row in db.scalars(select(model).where(model.member_id == remove_id)):
        content_id = getattr(row, id_field)
        extras = {field: getattr(row, field) for field in extra_fields}
        db.delete(row)
        if content_id in keep_ids:
            continue
        keep_ids.add(content_id)
        to_add.append({id_field: content_id, "member_id": keep_id, **extras})
    db.flush()
    for kwargs in to_add:
        db.add(model(**kwargs))


def _transfer_diseases(db: Session, keep_id: str, remove_id: str) -> None:
    """Move ``remove``'s disease records onto ``keep``, deduping by name.

    Mirrors the tree-merge dedup policy (``app.services.merge``, diseases
    section): two rows naming the same condition on the same person are
    noise once the two records describe one person, so the duplicate is
    dropped rather than kept alongside.
    """
    keep_names = {
        _norm(d.name)
        for d in db.scalars(
            select(MemberDisease).where(MemberDisease.member_id == keep_id)
        )
    }
    for disease in db.scalars(
        select(MemberDisease).where(MemberDisease.member_id == remove_id)
    ):
        name_key = _norm(disease.name)
        if name_key in keep_names:
            db.delete(disease)
            continue
        keep_names.add(name_key)
        disease.member_id = keep_id


def merge_members_in_place(
    db: Session,
    tree: Tree,
    keep: Member,
    remove: Member,
    fields: dict[str, str],
) -> tuple[Member, dict, Tree | None]:
    """Merge ``remove`` into ``keep`` within ``tree``; caller commits.

    Returns ``(keep, activity_details, counterpart_tree)`` — ``counterpart_tree``
    is set only when a tree-in-tree bridge link was re-wired, so the route can
    fire a ``tree.content_changed`` event for that other tree too.
    """
    if keep.id == remove.id:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400, detail="Cannot merge a member with itself"
        )

    normalized_fields = {
        snake: choice
        for snake, choice in (
            (_to_snake_case(field), choice) for field, choice in fields.items()
        )
        if snake in CONFLICT_FIELDS
    }

    # --- Cycle guard: simulate folding remove's edges onto keep first -------
    all_relations = list(
        db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == tree.id))
    )
    simulated_relations = []
    for r in all_relations:
        f = keep.id if r.from_member_id == remove.id else r.from_member_id
        t = keep.id if r.to_member_id == remove.id else r.to_member_id
        if f == t:
            continue
        simulated_relations.append(
            SimpleNamespace(from_member_id=f, to_member_id=t, relation_type=r.relation_type)
        )
    remaining_members = [
        m
        for m in db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree.id))
        if m.id != remove.id
    ]
    if find_parent_cycle_members(remaining_members, simulated_relations):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail="This merge would create a relationship cycle",
        )

    # --- Pre-image for the activity log, captured before any mutation -------
    counterpart: Member | None = (
        db.get(Member, remove.linked_member_id)
        if remove.linked_member_id is not None
        else None
    )
    removed_snapshot = member_delete_snapshot(db, remove, counterpart)["snapshot"]
    keep_before = {field: getattr(keep, field) for field in CONFLICT_FIELDS}

    # --- Field resolution onto keep (keep=clone=ma, remove=mb) --------------
    apply_field_choices(keep, keep, remove, normalized_fields)

    # --- Relations: union onto keep, dedupe, drop self-relations -----------
    keep_keys: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()
    remove_relations: list[Relation] = []
    for r in all_relations:
        if remove.id in (r.from_member_id, r.to_member_id):
            remove_relations.append(r)
        else:
            keep_keys.add((r.from_member_id, r.to_member_id, r.relation_type))

    new_relations: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
    for r in remove_relations:
        f = keep.id if r.from_member_id == remove.id else r.from_member_id
        t = keep.id if r.to_member_id == remove.id else r.to_member_id
        db.delete(r)
        if f == t:
            continue  # self-relation once both ends fold onto keep
        key = (f, t, r.relation_type)
        if key in keep_keys:
            continue  # keep already has this relation
        keep_keys.add(key)
        new_relations.append(key)
    db.flush()
    for f, t, relation_type in new_relations:
        db.add(
            Relation(
                tree_id=tree.id,
                from_member_id=f,
                to_member_id=t,
                relation_type=relation_type,
            )
        )

    # --- Content links: union onto keep, dedupe ------------------------------
    _repoint_member_links(db, EventMemberLink, "event_id", keep.id, remove.id)
    _repoint_member_links(db, StoryMemberLink, "story_id", keep.id, remove.id)
    _repoint_member_links(
        db,
        GalleryMemberLink,
        "gallery_image_id",
        keep.id,
        remove.id,
        extra_fields=("x", "y", "w", "h"),
    )
    _repoint_member_links(db, DocumentMemberLink, "document_id", keep.id, remove.id)
    _repoint_member_links(db, MemberTaskLink, "task_id", keep.id, remove.id)
    _transfer_diseases(db, keep.id, remove.id)

    # --- Tree-in-tree bridge: carry the link onto keep, else dissolve it ----
    counterpart_tree: Tree | None = None
    if counterpart is not None:
        if keep.linked_member_id is None:
            keep.linked_tree_id = remove.linked_tree_id
            keep.linked_member_id = remove.linked_member_id
            counterpart.linked_tree_id = keep.tree_id
            counterpart.linked_member_id = keep.id
        else:
            counterpart.linked_tree_id = None
            counterpart.linked_member_id = None
        counterpart_tree = db.get(Tree, counterpart.tree_id)

    details = {
        "merge": {
            "version": SNAPSHOT_VERSION,
            "keep_id": keep.id,
            "removed": removed_snapshot,
            "keep_before": keep_before,
            "field_choices": normalized_fields,
        }
    }

    db.delete(remove)
    return keep, details, counterpart_tree

@router.post("/members/merge", response_model=MemberOut)
def merge_members(
    payload: MemberMergeRequest,
    tree: Tree = Depends(get_writable_tree),
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Merge two members of this tree in place (#729).

    ``keep_id`` survives; ``remove_id`` is deleted after its relations,
    content links, and diseases are re-pointed onto ``keep_id`` and its
    conflicting fields are resolved per ``fields`` (a/b/combine, same
    semantics as the tree-merge resolver). Declared above
    ``/members/{member_id}`` — like ``positions``/``collapsed`` — so the
    literal ``merge`` path segment isn't captured as a member id.
    """
    keep = _get_member(db, tree, payload.keep_id)
    remove = _get_member(db, tree, payload.remove_id)
    merged, details, counterpart_tree = merge_members_in_place(
        db, tree, keep, remove, payload.fields
    )
    label = " ".join(filter(None, [merged.first_name, merged.last_name])) or None
    record_activity(
        db,
        tree_id=tree.id,
        actor=user,
        action="update",
        target_type="member",
        target_id=merged.id,
        target_label=label,
        details=details,
    )
    db.commit()
    publish_tree_event(db, tree, "activity.entry_added", {"tree_id": tree.id})
    db.refresh(merged)
    publish_tree_event(
        db,
        tree,
        "tree.content_changed",
        {"tree_id": tree.id, "domain": "member"},
    )
    invalidate_stats(tree.id)
    if counterpart_tree is not None:
        publish_tree_event(
            db,
            counterpart_tree,
            "tree.content_changed",
            {"tree_id": counterpart_tree.id, "domain": "member"},
        )
        invalidate_stats(counterpart_tree.id)
    return merged

"""Tests for the in-place, same-tree member merge (#729)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

from sqlalchemy import select

from app.models import (
    DocumentMemberLink,
    EventMemberLink,
    GalleryMemberLink,
    Member,
    MemberDisease,
    MemberTaskLink,
    Relation,
    StoryMemberLink,
)
from app.models.activity import ActivityLog
from app.models.content import (
    Document,
    Event,
    GalleryImage,
    MemberTask,
    Story,
)
from app.services.member_merge import (
    compute_member_merge_preview,
    merge_members_in_place,
)
from tests.conftest import API, add_member, make_tree, make_user, share

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Preview
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_preview_reports_camel_case_conflicts_and_transfer_counts(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    tree = make_tree(db, user, "T")
    keep = add_member(
        db, tree, "keep", first_name="Henry", last_name="Miller", gender="m",
        date_of_birth="1920", additional_data="Note A", birthplace="Berlin",
    )
    remove = add_member(
        db, tree, "remove", first_name="Henry", last_name="Miller", gender="m",
        date_of_birth="1920", additional_data="Note B", birthplace="Hamburg",
    )
    db.add(Relation(tree_id=tree.id, from_member_id="child", to_member_id="remove",
                     relation_type="parent"))
    add_member(db, tree, "child", first_name="Child", last_name="Miller")
    db.commit()

    preview = compute_member_merge_preview(db, tree, keep, remove)

    assert preview.pair.match == "exact"
    assert "additionalData" in preview.pair.conflicts
    assert "birthplace" in preview.pair.conflicts
    # snake_case names must not leak through
    assert "additional_data" not in preview.pair.conflicts
    assert preview.transfer.relations == 1

# Guard rails
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_self_merge_rejected(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    tree = make_tree(db, user, "T")
    keep = add_member(db, tree, "keep", first_name="A")

    from fastapi import HTTPException
    import pytest

    with pytest.raises(HTTPException) as exc:
        merge_members_in_place(db, tree, keep, keep, {})
    assert exc.value.status_code == 400


def test_route_rejects_cross_tree_members(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")

    tree_b = make_tree(db, user, "B")
    add_member(db, tree_a, "keep", first_name="A")
    add_member(db, tree_b, "remove", first_name="B")

    from app.db.session import get_db
    from fastapi import FastAPI

    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
    client = TestClient(app)

    from tests.conftest import auth

    resp = client.post(
        f"{API}/trees/{tree_a.id}/members/merge",
        json={"keep_id": "keep", "remove_id": "remove", "fields": {}},
        headers=auth(user),
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 404


def test_merge_creates_cycle_is_rejected(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    tree = make_tree(db, user, "T")
    # keep is remove's parent, and remove is keep's grandparent through a
    # third member — merging keep into remove would fold "keep is remove's
    # parent" and "remove is grandparent of keep" into a self-referencing
    # parent edge.
    keep = add_member(db, tree, "keep", first_name="Keep")
    remove = add_member(db, tree, "remove", first_name="Remove")
    mid = add_member(db, tree, "mid", first_name="Mid")
    db.add(Relation(tree_id=tree.id, from_member_id="remove", to_member_id="keep",
                     relation_type="parent"))
    db.add(Relation(tree_id=tree.id, from_member_id="mid", to_member_id="remove",
                     relation_type="parent"))
    db.add(Relation(tree_id=tree.id, from_member_id="keep", to_member_id="mid",
                     relation_type="parent"))
    db.commit()

    from fastapi import HTTPException
    import pytest

    with pytest.raises(HTTPException) as exc:
        merge_members_in_place(db, tree, keep, remove, {})
    assert exc.value.status_code == 400

def test_relation_repointed_onto_keep(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    tree = make_tree(db, user, "T")
    keep = add_member(db, tree, "keep", first_name="Keep")
    remove = add_member(db, tree, "remove", first_name="Remove")
    add_member(db, tree, "child", first_name="Child")
    db.add(Relation(tree_id=tree.id, from_member_id="child", to_member_id="remove",
                     relation_type="parent"))
    db.commit()

    merge_members_in_place(db, tree, keep, remove, {})
    db.commit()

    relations = db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == tree.id)).all()
    assert len(relations) == 1
    assert relations[0].from_member_id == "child"
    assert relations[0].to_member_id == "keep"

    user = make_user(db, "alice")

    remove = add_member(db, tree, "remove", first_name="Remove")

                     relation_type="parent"))
    db.add(Relation(tree_id=tree.id, from_member_id="child", to_member_id="remove",
                     relation_type="parent"))
    db.commit()

    merge_members_in_place(db, tree, keep, remove, {})
    db.commit()

    relations = db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == tree.id)).all()
    assert len(relations) == 1
    assert relations[0].to_member_id == "keep"


def test_self_relation_is_dropped(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    tree = make_tree(db, user, "T")
    keep = add_member(db, tree, "keep", first_name="Keep")
    remove = add_member(db, tree, "remove", first_name="Remove")
    db.add(Relation(tree_id=tree.id, from_member_id="remove", to_member_id="keep",

    db.commit()

    merge_members_in_place(db, tree, keep, remove, {})
    db.commit()

    relations = db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == tree.id)).all()
    assert relations == []

gh pr create --title "feat(quality): guided in-place merge for duplicate member candidates" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Connects two previously-separate subsystems per #729: the quality report's
`duplicate_candidate` findings (which only offered *dismiss*) and the
tree-merge field-conflict machinery (`compute_merge_preview` /
`apply_field_choices` from #166), so a duplicate finding can now be resolved
with a guided **in-place** merge of two members of the same tree.

- **Backend**: `GET /trees/{id}/members/{id}/merge-preview` and
  `POST /trees/{id}/members/merge` (`keep_id`, `remove_id`, `fields`), backed
  by a new `member_merge` service that:
  - reuses `compute_conflicts` / `apply_field_choices` from the existing
    tree-merge service rather than forking the logic;
  - unions relations and content links (events, stories, gallery, documents,
    research tasks, diseases) onto the kept member, **deduping** instead of
    raising an integrity error when the union would produce a duplicate row,
    and dropping relations that become self-referencing once both ends fold
    onto the same member;
  - refuses to merge a member with itself, and refuses a merge that would
    create a relationship cycle — the cycle-detection DFS is extracted out of
    `quality_checks.run_quality_checks` into `find_parent_cycle_members` so
    the report and the merge guard agree on what counts as a cycle;
  - carries a tree-in-tree bridge link onto the kept member when only the
    removed member had one, otherwise dissolves it (mirroring the existing
    single-member-delete behavior);
  - records a rich `record_activity` payload (full pre-image of the removed
    member + its relations/links/diseases, plus the kept member's
    pre-resolution field values) so a future undo feature (#572) has enough
    to work with.
- **Frontend**: a "Merge…" action on `duplicate_candidate` findings in
  `QualityReportView` opens `MergeMembersDialog`, which reuses the existing
  `MergeConflictResolver` (already shared with the tree-in-tree linking flow)
  for side-by-side field resolution, shows a preview of what will transfer,
  and lets the user pick which two members to merge when a finding lists more
  than two same-named members.
- Entry point lives behind the existing `quality_report` feature flag (the
  quality report view is already gated); the merge/preview endpoints
  themselves are core member CRUD and are **not** separately flagged, per the
  issue's guidance.
- CHANGELOG entry added under `Unreleased`.

## Test plan

- [x] Backend: `uv run ruff check`, `uv run pytest -n auto` (full suite, incl.
      new `tests/test_member_merge.py` covering relation re-pointing +
      dedup-on-duplicate, self-relation drop, per-table content-link
      transfer, disease dedup, self-merge/cross-tree/cycle guards, field
      resolution (b/combine), and the activity-log payload shape)
- [x] Frontend: `npm run build` (tsc + vite), `npx vitest run` (full suite,
      incl. new `MergeMembersDialog.test.tsx`), `npm run check-i18n`

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)"
